transaction_contract_note: forwardAuth plus its mandatory private-UDS response observer use the same opaque-handle Common P3/P4 companion contract; Native UDS maps all phases directly through Common Runtime.

logical_transaction_contract.scope: The legacy capability table below describes the direct request-only forwardAuth service. This object describes the required complete logical connector and must be used for P1-P4 contract assessment.

phases.P1: forwardAuth authorization service maps request headers into Common Runtime
phases.P2: forwardAuth buffers the bounded request body with forwardBody=true and maxBodySize=4096, then the authorization service supplies the configured Common request EOS
phases.P3: following private-UDS response-observer plugin claims the opaque handle and maps response headers before writer commitment
phases.P4: same observer maps bounded response chunks and exactly one EOS through MRC1

logical_transaction_contract.correlation: server-generated 256-bit opaque handle; one claim; transaction and host IDs remain internal
logical_transaction_contract.failure_behavior: missing observer, malformed/replayed handle, MRC1 error, deadline, or cleanup failure is fail-closed

external_references.title: Traefik Proxy v3.7 ForwardAuth configuration
external_references.supports: forwardBody enables buffered request-body forwarding; maxBodySize bounds it; forwarding the body breaks streaming

host_model_constraints: The forwardAuth service alone observes the authorization request before upstream handling; the mandatory following response-observer plugin receives the corresponding response headers and streaming body.

Traefik v3.7 supports buffered forwardAuth request bodies with forwardBody and maxBodySize; the checked-in dynamic configuration enables both with a 4096-byte cap and the service config requires request_body_mode=buffered.
Traefik documents that forwardBody buffering breaks streaming, so streaming request-body inspection is outside this host path.
The authorization service currently sees the Traefik-to-service socket endpoints and does not map original client connection endpoints into Common connection metadata.

The full-lifecycle profile separately selects native-middleware through full-lifecycle-traefik-native in a pinned Traefik local-plugin host probe. Its selected UDS engine service performs Common/libmodsecurity evaluation, while this forwardAuth compatibility declaration remains separate and unpromoted.
The opaque response handle is propagated only from forwardAuth to the following local response observer and is removed before the upstream handler; missing observer or correlation is fail-closed.
